#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#             then vlinux
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#   vlinux    build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf (the vlinux proxy-kernel
#             skeleton, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md; depends on the runtime
#             lib, built automatically)
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime|vlinux] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures"; run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
  vlinux)   run make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" ;;
esac

105	  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"

111	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"

135	default_jobs() {
136	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap

161	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
162	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
163	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE

165	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
166	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
167	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
168	run_one() {

171	  local start end elapsed status rc
172	  start=$(date +%s)

174	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1

177	  end=$(date +%s)

180	    0)  status=PASS ;;
181	    77) status=SKIP ;;
182	    *)  status=FAIL ;;

186	    case "$status" in

237	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
238	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
239	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo

259	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"

261	  ) &
262	done

264	exec 8>&-

266	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
267	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
268	  i=$((i+1))
269	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
270	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
271	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
272	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
273	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
274	done

276	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
277	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
279	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

281	  case "$r_status" in
282	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
283	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
284	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
285	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
286	  esac
287	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
288	
289	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
290	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
291	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
292	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
293	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
294	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"

296	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts
# (source ./setup.sh first to export the external qemu/vsim locations).
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under $VSIM_BIN_DIR)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); empty when setup.sh has not run -- the require below reports it.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under $VSIM_BIN_DIR -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

2	"""Classify every spec CSR by its hybrid-handoff transport disposition.
3	
4	The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
5	snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
6	and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
7	single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.
8	
9	The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
10	The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
11	two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
12	fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.
13	
14	Dispositions:
15	  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
16	  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
17	  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
18	  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
19	  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange
20	  EXCL_RV32      RV32 high-half shadow -- irrelevant on RV64
21	  EXCL_SIDEFX    read/write has side effects -- not architectural state
22	  EXCL_W1C_HW    write-1-clear, hardware-driven (like mip)
23	  EXCL_INDIRECT  miselect/mireg access mechanism, not a direct register
24	  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
25	  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives
26	  EXCL_MODE      S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope
27	  EXCL_TRAP      detailed trap-cause latch, live only after a trap
28	
29	Usage:
30	  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv>            # write csr_coverage.csv beside it
31	  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv> --stdout   # print, do not write
32	"""
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import csv
36	import sys
37	from pathlib import Path
38	
39	# CSRs already carried in hybrid_state_v1 today (Bucket A). Names as the spec
40	# summary tables print them (range rows kept verbatim, e.g. pmpaddr1~63).
41	TRANSPORT_NOW = {
42	    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
43	    "mideleg", "mie", "mip", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr", "frm",
44	    "fﬂags",  # "fflags" with the fi-ligature the PDF emits
45	    "JVT", "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl", "mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl",
46	    "milmb", "mdlmb", "mecc_code", "mhsp_ctl", "msp_bound", "msp_base",
47	    "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "ucode",
48	    "pmpcfg0", "pmpcfg1", "pmpcfg2", "pmpcfg3", "pmpcfg4~15",
49	    "pmpaddr0", "pmpaddr1~63",
50	    "pmacfg0", "pmacfg2", "pmaaddr0~47",
51	}
52	
53	# Per-name decisions that override the structural defaults below.
54	OVERRIDE = {
55	    "misa": "CONST_RO", "tinfo": "CONST_RO", "tdata3": "CONST_RO",
56	    "mintstatus": "EXCL_RO",

The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.

Dispositions:
  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange

  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives
  EXCL_MODE      S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope

  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv> --stdout   # print, do not write

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Classify every spec CSR by its hybrid-handoff transport disposition.

The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.

Dispositions:
  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange
  EXCL_RV32      RV32 high-half shadow -- irrelevant on RV64
  EXCL_SIDEFX    read/write has side effects -- not architectural state
  EXCL_W1C_HW    write-1-clear, hardware-driven (like mip)
  EXCL_INDIRECT  miselect/mireg access mechanism, not a direct register
  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

_hybrid_setup_main "$@"
unset -f _hybrid_setup_main 2>/dev/null
unset _SETUP_SRC

#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 4).
#
# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }

# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
fi
[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"

# rv64 (required).
if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi
make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"

# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
else
  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
fi
